headline: Massachusetts awards $2.25 million for re-entry job training
dek: Twelve organizations will help 445 formerly incarcerated residents pursue training, career support and jobs in fields including construction, manufacturing, health care and hospitality.
body: Massachusetts is awarding $2.25 million in grants to 12 organizations that will provide job training, career support and employment opportunities for 445 formerly incarcerated residents returning to their communities, the state said Thursday.

The programs will connect participants with employers in construction, manufacturing, culinary and hospitality, health care, transportation and other fields. The grants are part of the Re-Entry Workforce Development Demonstration Program, which is administered by the Commonwealth Corporation through the Executive Office of Labor and Workforce Development.

Project Place in Boston received $200,000 to train 50 returning residents for work in transportation and warehousing, maintenance and manufacturing. The state said successful graduates will be placed with employers including the New Market Business Improvement District and Aramark.

Since January 2023, Massachusetts and the Commonwealth Corporation have awarded nearly $10 million through the program, with the investments projected to serve more than 1,400 people as they re-enter their communities. The latest grants were funded through the state's fiscal 2026 workforce-development budget.
